title: Functions and signatures
summary: Every parameter needs a type; the return type is part of the contract.
lecture: A Rust function spells out its full contract: `fn greeting(name: &str) -> String`. Parameter types are mandatory - there is no inference at function boundaries - and the return type comes after `->`. Omit it and the function returns `()`.

The body's last expression is the return value. A mismatch between the promised return type and what the body actually produces is error E0308, and the fix is usually a missing type, a stray semicolon, or the wrong expression at the end.
Calling a function with the wrong number or types of arguments fails at compile time (E0061, E0308). Nothing is coerced behind your back.

example.caption: Parameter typed, return typed, body ends in an expression.
